baseline_withdrawals.scope: Inherited v0.17 projects removed from the selection by a pinned schema-v3 baseline withdrawal, because their selected evidence does not meet the acceptance contract. A withdrawal removes the project row, its single-project site row and GeoJSON feature, and every evidence row only it referenced; every other inherited byte is unchanged. It asserts no physical status: a withdrawn project is not claimed to be paused, cancelled, completed or not under construction, and its physical status on the lifecycle reference date is unknown. It neither changes nor re-reviews other rows: selected rows that share a withdrawn row's source capture (the same source URL and content hash) stay selected unchanged, are acknowledged in each record's shared_capture_rows, and keep the withdrawal_shared_capture_review gate open. ATTRIBUTION.txt keeps every inherited v0.17 notice, including notices for sources that only withdrawn rows used. A site-count claim must disclose withdrawals.

blind_review.counted_session_rule: At each position the counted session is the completed blind session with the lowest session_sequence; a blind session attests no Atlas access and cites no Atlas surface in its evidence or location URLs. Every other session is recorded uncounted with a machine-checked reason: aborted (no reviewer output), blindness_breach (attested Atlas access or a cited Atlas surface) or later_duplicate (a blind session started after the counted one).

Those reviewers fell back on first-party sites, registers and publisher listings. The two disagreements, positions 10 and 17, are among them, so their unable_to_verify determinations may reflect search capacity rather than an Atlas error; the versioned reviews of those rows address that.

The 0-1 m distances (positions 7, 14, 15, 17 and 19) and the in-polygon point at position 4 trace to the same official or first-party sources the Atlas uses, except at position 7, where two independent sources mark the same building centre.

Structural weakness: the blind sessions shared one session scratchpad with the orchestrator, which held Atlas working material. The comparator's audit found no blind-session reference to any of it. One helper was used across sessions: reviewer 5 wrote an HTML-to-text helper, h2t.py, to the scratchpad root at 16:20:39Z, and reviewers 9 (at 16:24:29Z) and 14 (at 16:32:48Z) each ran it in one command, on two of their own captures, when the shell's noclobber setting stopped them overwriting it with a helper of their own. The comparator's audit, which looked for references to scratchpad entries older than the referencing session, missed reviewer 9's use because session 9 started 18 s before the helper existed. The helper only converts HTML to text and holds no Atlas data.

The comparator computed the same rows with pyproj 3.7.1 (Karney geodesic) and shapely 2.1.1; the two agree to better than 1 mm at every located position (largest difference 0.000007 m), and every construction, location and agreement verdict equals the comparator's. Where the reviewer point lies inside the site polygon or is exactly the site Point (positions 4, 5, 15, 17, 18, 20), the builder's rule is inside; the comparator's working record labels those rows agree_within_1000m. No row falls in the 1,000-3,000 m band, so no adjudication was made. Stage-level differences inside 'under construction' are recorded in the comparison notes and, as pre-registered, do not count as disagreement.

Reviewer fields with no slot here (date_semantics, date_semantics_note, stage_observed, capture_path, source_crs_and_transformation and what_the_point_represents) are copied verbatim into the evidence item's note or the location's notes; sources_searched is kept only in reviewer_output. Each is recorded with a day its own value states or bounds, chosen so that the item counts as inside the 2026-05-22..2026-08-20 window only if every day the value allows is inside it: the latest day the value allows, except that a value that begins before the window and reaches into it takes its earliest day; an undated page takes the capture day its reviewer gives. The original value is kept in the item's note. Recorded: position 5 item 5: '2026-06' -> 2026-06-30 (inside); position 7 item 2: '2026-08' -> 2026-08-31 (outside); position 10 item 0: 'undated (captured 2026-10-09)' -> 2026-10-09 (outside); position 13 item 2: '2026-02 (photo); published 2026-03-12' -> 2026-03-12 (outside); position 13 item 5: '2026-01-21 (recorded works start); record state as captured 2026-10-09' -> 2026-01-21 (outside); position 14 item 1: '2026-06' -> 2026-06-30 (inside); position 18 item 1: '2026-05 (published 2026-05-12..2026-06-02)' -> 2026-05-12 (outside). Each result is consistent with its reviewer's own reading of the window (the reviewers of positions 5 and 14 place their items inside it; the others do not rely on theirs as in-window observations), and no determination depends on these items: every under_construction_in_window session also has an exactly dated in-window item.

blind_review.location_method: Against the site geometry of the pre-registered population release, in WGS84: a point covered by a Polygon/MultiPolygon in longitude/latitude (RFC 7946 straight edges, boundary inclusive, holes excluded) or equal to a Point is inside at 0 m; otherwise the minimum ellipsoidal geodesic distance (Vincenty inverse, converged to 1e-12 rad; mean-sphere great circle if a nearly antipodal pair does not converge) to the Point or to any ring edge, minimized along each edge by golden-section search with both endpoints checked. within_1000m: 0 < d <= 1000 m; adjudication band: 1000 < d <= 3000 m; beyond_3000m: d > 3000 m. The rule is classified from the recomputed distance; a recorded distance must agree with it within max(5 m, 1 %) and lie in the same band (exactly 0 m for inside).

Its result is reported but cannot pass this checkpoint's gate; a new pre-registered sample of the current eligible population is required.

A site-count claim must disclose them.
